subtitle.zh-TW: 只有心理病態者才會按這個按鈕，所以想按本身就是壞消息。
subtitle.en: Only a psychopath would press this button, so the urge to press is itself bad news.

story.zh-TW: 考慮保羅正在決定要不要按下「殺光所有心理病態者」按鈕的情境。他認為世界上沒有心理病態者會好得多，但更看重自己活著，寧可活在有心理病態者的世界，也不願死去。他相當確信，只有心理病態者才會去按這樣的按鈕。
story.en: Consider Paul, who is deciding whether to press a button that kills all psychopaths. He thinks a world without psychopaths would be much better, but he values his own life more and would rather live among psychopaths than die. He is quite confident that only a psychopath would press such a button.

zh-TW.sentence: 考慮保羅正在決定要不要按下「殺光所有心理病態者」按鈕的情境。
他相當確信，只有心理病態者才會去按這樣的按鈕。

en.sentence: Consider Paul, who is deciding whether to press a button that kills all psychopaths.
He is quite confident that only a psychopath would press such a button.

text.zh-TW: 想按的人多半是心理病態者，按下去保羅自己也會死，所以不按才合理。
text.en: Whoever wants to press is probably a psychopath and would die of it; refraining is the rational choice.

explanation.zh-TW: 外生變數（exogenous variable）是保羅是否為心理病態者 PSY，以及非病態者偶爾也想按的衝動 U_P。兩者任一出現，保羅就按下按鈕（PRESS）；他按了而且是心理病態者，就會死（DIE）。保羅原本認為自己是病態者的機率很低。對 PRESS 作干預（intervention）時，多半是非病態者按下，因果決策論（causal decision theory）算出按下有利。得知自己按了，幾乎就是得知自己是病態者，證據決策論（evidential decision theory）算出按下會死。Egan 沒有給數字，效用（活著且病態者消失 10、死亡 −100、不按 0）與機率由本資料集所擬。
explanation.en: The exogenous variables are whether Paul is a psychopath, PSY, and an occasional urge to press even in a non-psychopath, U_P. Pressing PRESS is brought about by either; Paul's death DIE needs that he pressed and that he is a psychopath. Paul starts out thinking it very unlikely that he is a psychopath, so intervening on PRESS most likely means a non-psychopath presses and the psychopaths disappear, and causal decision theory finds pressing better. But learning that he pressed is nearly learning that he is a psychopath, and evidential decision theory finds that pressing means death. Egan gives no numbers; the utilities (alive with the psychopaths gone 10, death −100, not pressing 0) and the probabilities are chosen to keep the model minimal. Egan notes that this case draws fewer dissenters than the Murder Lesion.

sources.citation: Egan, A. (2007). Some counterexamples to causal decision theory. Philosophical Review, 116(1), 93–114.
sources.pages: 97 (case, intuition and n. 3), 98 (the needed low credence in being a psychopath), 107 (ratifiability), 109 (neither option ratifiable)

note.zh-TW: p. 98 說明：CDT 要建議按下，保羅原本認為自己是心理病態者的機率必須夠低；這個情境由 David Braddon-Mitchell 提出（p. 97 註 2）。
note.en: Egan (p. 98) notes that for causal decision theory to advise pressing, Paul's prior credence that he is a psychopath must be low enough; the case was suggested by David Braddon-Mitchell (p. 97, n. 2).

label.en: Urge to press without being a psychopath

verdicts.note: Pressing is strong evidence of being a psychopath.
Intervening on the press leaves PSY at its prior.
Once Paul takes himself to be about to press, pressing looks fatal: unratifiable (Egan p. 107).
Once Paul takes himself to refrain he is no psychopath and pressing would be safe: refraining is unratifiable too (Egan p. 109).
